title: Whole-Program Analysis
description: Analyzes all modules together at link time instead of one file at a time, seeing the complete call graph. Whole-program visibility enables optimizations that are impossible per-file, like inlining across module boundaries and proving a function has only one caller.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Cross-Module Inlining
description: Inlines small functions across module boundaries, removing call overhead and exposing the combined code to further optimization. LTO inlining is guided by cost models so it speeds up hot paths without bloating the binary with inlined cold code.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Dead Code Elimination
description: Removes functions and globals unreachable from the program entry points, proven dead by the whole-program call graph. DCE at link time catches dead code that spans modules, which per-file compilation can never see.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Interprocedural Constant Propagation
description: Propagates constant values across function boundaries, so a function always called with the same argument gets specialized as if the value were hardcoded. The specialization then unlocks further folding and branch elimination inside the function.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Function Outlining
description: Extracts repeated code sequences into shared functions, trading a little call overhead for smaller binaries. Outlining is the size-optimizer's counterpart to inlining: where inlining trades size for speed, outlining trades speed for size.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Identical Code Folding
description: Merges functions with byte-identical bodies into a single copy, a classic size win for template-heavy and generated code. Folding is safe because identical bodies behave identically; debug info keeps the original names for stack traces.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Link-Time Devirtualization
description: Resolves virtual calls to direct calls when whole-program analysis proves only one implementation can be reached. Devirtualized calls can then be inlined, turning expensive indirect dispatch into straight-line code on hot paths.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Profile-Guided Layout
description: Orders functions in the binary by execution profile so hot code sits together, improving instruction-cache locality. Better cache behavior means fewer stalls, which shows up directly as faster startup and steadier frame rates.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Symbol Visibility Control
description: Marks internal symbols hidden so the linker can discard and optimize them aggressively, exporting only the public API. Hidden symbols enable more inlining and DCE, and they shrink dynamic symbol tables for faster loading.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Thin LTO
description: Splits LTO into a fast thin-link step using per-module summaries, then parallel backend compilation. ThinLTO delivers most of full LTO's gains with build times close to normal compilation, making link-time optimization practical for everyday development.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Section Garbage Collection
description: Places each function and variable in its own section so the linker can discard unreferenced sections individually. Section GC is the linker's fine-grained dead-code elimination, and it pairs with compiler flags that enable per-function sections.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Call-Graph Pruning
description: Removes call-graph edges proven impossible - dead virtual targets, guarded branches never taken - so later passes optimize a smaller, truer graph. Pruning compounds: each removed edge can unlock more inlining and more dead code.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Alias Analysis
description: Determines which pointers can reference the same memory, letting the optimizer reorder and eliminate loads and stores safely. Precise alias information is the foundation of most loop and memory optimizations - without it, the compiler must assume the worst.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Loop Distribution
description: Splits a loop with mixed work into separate loops so each can be vectorized or parallelized independently. Distribution at link time sees the whole program's loop nests, enabling splits that per-file compilation cannot prove safe.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Binary Size Budgets
description: Sets per-component size limits enforced at link time, failing the build when a component grows past its budget. Size budgets make bloat visible at the commit that introduces it, when it is cheapest to fix.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
